newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 6.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Federal Government looks set to announce in next week's Budget that it will have a zero bond-financing requirement for next year, meaning it will not have to borrow any funds on financial markets in 1997-98. Private-sector analysts are also predicting the Coalition will achieve big "headline" Budget surpluses this financial year and in 1997-98. Page 1.

In a letter to Federal Communications Minister Richard Alston, the Coalition's backbench communications committee expressed strong opposition to further media concentration and demanded no public announcement of a Cabinet decision on changes to media owneship rules be made until the backbench had been consulted. Page 3.

According to the ANZ Banking Group's latest employment advertising series, job vacancies increased by 2.5 per cent in trend terms in April. The result is the largest such increase in almost three years, and suggests the economy will create 50,000 new jobs over the next three months, although the Howard Government will still fall short of its 1.5 per cent employment growth target. Page 5.

Australia and Germany developed new bilateral cultural and science projects during Prime Minister John Howard's first meeting with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl in Canberra yesterday. Howard said Australia's focus on the Asia-Pacific did not preclude a deep association with Europe and Germany and Kohl also stressed the importance of links between Australia, Europe and Germany. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In his first interview since the Australian Federal Police began investigating his affairs last month, embattled Independent Senator Mal Colston threatened to jeopardise the Budget, media ownership reforms, and superannuation changes, saying he had no choice but to vote against the Federal Government. Page 1.

Several Federal Government MPs yesterday backed plans by Prime Minister John Howard for a direct criticism of controversial Independent MP Pauline Hanson and her One Nation party. The move followed the release of the latest Newspoll, which revealed support for the Coalition is at its lowest level in more than two years, while support for One Nation has increased by six percentage points in the past month. Page 1.

In a development which comes as Seven Network chairman Kerry Stokes warned the Federal Government yesterday not to allow Kerry Packer to control the John Fairfax publishing group, a consortium of Australian institutions, backed by prominent United Kingdom publisher Pearson Plc, has emerged to rival Packer's bid. Page 1.

Speaking after holding talks with Prime Minister John Howard over the possibility of economic and political co-operation in both Asia and Europe, German Chancellor Dr Helmut Kohl yesterday strongly supported Australia's bid to overcome exclusion from summit meetings of Asian and European leaders. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

According to a Herald AGB-McNair poll conducted last weekend, controversial Independent MP Pauline Hanson's One Nation party has attracted 10 per cent of primary votes after just three weeks. The survey revealed the party has attracted many of the battler the Howard Government won over at the last election - and has returned them to the Australian Labor Party on preferences. Page 1.

While Seven Network chairman Kerry Stokes announced yesterday he would consider buying into John Fairfax Holdings Ltd if media ownership restrictions were changed, Prime Minister John Howard was warned by his backbench yesterday of the danger of further cncentration of media ownership. The moves come on the eve of a possible Cabinet decision which would allow Nine Network owner Kerry Packer take over the Fairfax group. Page 1.

The National Australia Bank and the ANZ Bank both said yesterday the big increase in people using credit cards but avoiding accruing interest by quickly settling their balances meant increased fees were inevitable, with NAB announcing a new A$1 charge on credit card cash withdrawals. Page 1.

Prompted by an apparent shooting outbreak of protected Australian fur seals at Jervis Bay, which has seen four animals shot in the past week, State and Federal national parks and fisheries officials have organised an urgent meeting in Nowra today to discus investigations and possible prosecutions. Page 3.
THE AGE

Public confrontation over controversial MP Pauline Hanson and her One Nation party spread to Victoria last night when hundreds of protesters forced their way into a meeting in Geelong designed to establish a State branch of the party. The meeting was abandoned early after police expressed fears the protest would erupt into violence. Page 1.

In comments which come after the Federal Opposition and the Australian Democrats criticised apparent moves by the Coalition to reduce media ownership restrictions, Tasmanian Independent Brian Harradine, who holds the balance of power in the Senate, last night supported calls for media diversity. Page 1.

A deputation of Melbourne Football Club captain Garry Lyon and new chief executive Cameron Schwab met the Demons' president Joseph Gutnick yesterday in a bid to convince him Neil Balme should be retained as the club's coach. It is believed Gutnick was previously prepared to sack Balme. Page 1.

In seminars to be held today, the electricity industry's co-ordinator, the Victorian Power Exchange, plans to ask industry leaders for ideas on coping with another year of record hot weather which could put the State's power supply under pressure. The hot spell may see the Newport power station having to be reopened. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
